prompt: Vertical 9:16 night evidence photograph: a close tabletop shot looking down at about 50 degrees, as if someone fired an on-camera flash at the scene of a small family crime. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. It shows one hoop worn at true size, about a third of the ear's height; use reference 2 only for the piece and its true size, and take nothing else from it: not the person, her face, hair, skin or clothes. Preserve the earring exactly: one hinged round hoop of the pair, 20 x 18 mm, of 1 chunky 4-5 mm tube twisted like rope: about 4 broad, soft, rounded ridges across the band, smooth swells as in reference 1 with no seam lines between them, spiralling one way all round; 1 thin plain wire post, a fine wire far thinner than the tube, spans the top quarter from a plain smooth hinge into the other end; smooth inner face; 0 stones. Mirror-polished 18k gold tone, warm-neutral yellow; the wire post in the same 18k gold tone; never orange, copper or brassy under the lamp. Must stay a fat twisted rope tube, never a thin, braided or chain hoop, never a smooth plain hoop. Do not redesign, restyle, resize or add anything: nothing hangs from or touches the bottom of the hoop, no loop, bead, charm or stem. Only one hoop of the pair is in the frame; its hinge and fine wire post show plainly on its far side, so it reads at once as an earring, never as a ring. SCALE: the hoop is 20 mm tall, the size of a one-rupee coin, the tube as thick as a pencil; the frame is about 7 cm across at the hoop, so the hoop fills about 28% of the frame width. The scale referent beside it is the dropped hair tie: an ordinary black fabric hair tie, a slack loop about 45 mm across of 4 mm cord, so the hoop is a little less than half the tie's width and the rope tube is about as thick as the tie's cord; never a hoop as big as the hair tie. THE HAIR TIE is one seamless black fabric loop, soft knit fabric all the way round, with no metal joint, crimp, clip, band or bead anywhere on it and no metal of any kind. It lies just below the hoop and the print with a clear gap of dusted wood, about a finger's width, between its loop and the hoop's lower edge: it never touches the hoop. Last time the tie had a small gold metal crimp joint exactly where it touched the bottom of the hoop, and at phone size it looked like an invented loop hanging from the earring; that must not happen again. WORLD: an old walnut dressing table, fine grain and a few scratches, dusted with a thin, translucent film of spilled white talcum powder through which the dark grain still shows; never a white pile, never a pale field; under the flash the talc stays a thin grey-white veil, never blown to pure white. The hoop lies flat in the powder, a little left of centre, with a dark contact shadow, needle-sharp, every rope ridge readable, the brightest thing in the frame. Beside it, to its right, the print its twin left when it was lifted a minute ago: a clean ring of bare dark wood in the powder, exactly the size and round shape of the hoop beside it, with powder inside and outside the ring and crisp edges, empty. The print's bare band is as wide as the hoop's tube, about 5 mm, the full footprint of the lifted twin, never a thin pencil line; last time it was a thin 2 mm line. The print is a void, never a mound: flat bare wood, darker than the dusted wood around it, never a raised rim or ridge of powder, never a ghost or shadow of a hoop. THE PUFF: a soft pale pink round powder puff, out of focus, almost entirely beyond the frame: only its lower edge peeks in at the very top edge, in the top right corner, inside the top tenth of the frame; never beside the headline zone, never in the left half of the top third. Last time the puff sat large at the upper left, where the headline goes. No hands, no people. LIGHT: one hard direct on-camera flash just above the lens is the main light: flat frontal light, the look of a point-and-shoot flash photo, with crisp, hard-edged black drop shadows thrown down-right of every object and one small sharp white specular on each polished curve; never a soft, spotlit still life. Last time the light came out soft and spotlit with soft-edged shadows. A dim warm tungsten glow from a bedside lamp out of frame left only lifts the deepest shadows with a little amber. Flash held down so the metal never clips and every rope ridge stays readable. Beyond the flash the room falls to near-black. COMPOSITION: the hoop and the print sit side by side about half-way down the frame, the hair tie below them across its gap; the top third is calm near-black falloff for a headline, empty but for the puff's sliver in the top right corner; the bottom third is calm dusted walnut sinking into shadow, for a strip of type. GRADE: a real 35 mm night flash snapshot: velvety blacks with a faint oxblood cast, fine grain, slight vignette, true colour on the piece; candid, never glossy CGI. Full-bleed 9:16 photograph edge to edge; no borders, bands or panels. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no labels or printing on anything. No face, eyes, eyebrows or lips. Exactly one product, this one hoop; no other jewellery anywhere, no rings, bangles or watches on any hand, and no metal anywhere except the hoop. No second hoop, nothing inside the bare print.
